precise_conclusion: given any fixed finite (data, compute, prior) closure, a criterion 'a true subject satisfies it but the equal-access shadow cannot' is provably non-existent; the necessary condition can only possibly hold in fork A (non-stationary / generated access, where 'Bayes-optimal-given-access' is not a well-defined dominating object); fork A itself yields only un-shadowable mechanism evidence and does not cross the functional->phenomenal gap
